body: I'll create a reproducer, but I'd bet this test that you mention doesn't have `jackson-module-jaxb-annotations` on classpath.
Oh wait, I already created a reproducer, it's linked in the issue description :-) https://github.com/Ladicek/quarkus-test-serialization-issue.git
Oh, you're saying that loading that module changes the behaviour of jackson. Wow.
It's a `ServiceLoader` thing, if I remember correctly.

So I can't reproduce it in my test just by adding your import. Even in your project, serialisation is only broken when sending from the client to the server. It works from the server to the client.

So it's a bit more mysterious than that.
On the server it only checks for `@JsonIgnore` and `@Transient`. On the client it first checks for `@XmlTransient`, that's why the difference.
It's possible that the original test was for jaxb, and not jackson. I have to test this sort of stuff for jsonb, jaxb and jackson to make sure I get it right for all three.

OK, confirmed that this `@XmlTransient` is required by JAXB, but causes Jackson to ignore the property. I now have tests that check JAXB, JSONB and Jackson (with the JAXB module) and can reproduce. Just have to find a way to make all three work at the same time.
